argument_summary: The certification theory should be narrowed. On this record, aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance principles support only a limited claim that launch readiness is otherwise established and that monitored deployment is generally permissible. They do not by themselves prove that the internal disclosure predicate has been satisfied. The supportable position is therefore not clean compliance without qualification, but a caveated certification packet that preserves the unresolved materiality issue while recognizing that the record does contain meaningful readiness evidence.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy in this case is the materiality rule, not the general public governance guidance. The admissible record shows a 1.3-point miss in the small-business onboarding segment, that the segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, and that legal review remains open. Under the stated policy text, those facts make it difficult to treat the limitation as immaterial based only on a non-core or low-volume characterization. At the same time, the policy does not make aggregate readiness evidence irrelevant; it supports a narrower conclusion that the model may be technically ready overall even though the disclosure or risk-acceptance condition remains unresolved. The defensible audit treatment is therefore caveated compliance or equivalent narrowing of the packet, not an unqualified compliant finding on the present record.
claims_about_business_cost: Unnecessary escalation is not required to recognize the distinction between overall readiness evidence and unresolved policy predicates. A caveated treatment preserves launch-governance continuity and avoids overstating noncompliance where the record does show aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents. The business-cost point is limited: the ask is not to ignore the materiality concern, but to avoid treating the packet as if it claimed more than the admissible evidence can support.
concessions: The present record does not show that a required disclosure was made before launch.
The present record does not show approved risk acceptance covering the named segment gap.
Public AI-risk and model-card guidance do not override the specific internal materiality policy in the case record.
The named paid pilot commitments and open legal review materially weaken any claim of clean certification without qualification.
